rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sūrah directly identifies hypocrites whose practiced hypocrisy leaves no hope of reform; 9:80 extends the warning to seventy pleas for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: the character of those hypocrites who had become so seasoned in their hypocrisy that there was no hope of their reformation is under discussion here

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites use repeated oaths to persuade the Prophet that they believe.
rows.anchor: the hypocrites would try to convince the Prophet (sws) through repeated oaths

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated swearing responds to the distrust created by their continual blunders; they know people will not believe them without an oath.
rows.anchor: unless they swore on oath on what they said, no one would believe them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links habitual oath-taking to the Qur’an’s warning against the person who swears false oaths and is despicable.
rows.anchor: heed not every person who swears false oaths and who is despicable

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s messengership needs no human proof; God knows it, while His testimony exposes the hypocrites as liars.
rows.anchor: it does not need their proof. God knows fully that he is His messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oaths shield the hypocrites from scrutiny so they can appear loyal to Islam while continuing their schemes.
rows.anchor: these hypocrites use their oaths as shields; the purpose is that they continue to be considered sincere towards Islam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects their oath-based deception with their friendship and sworn assurances to the Jews, while they adopted the same policy with Muslims.
rows.anchor: they had deep ties of friendship with a people who had earned the wrath of God: the Jews

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel warning appears in al-Mujādalah 58:16 with slightly different wording and adds humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: this same verse also occurs there with a slight change in words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites think their oaths protect them from both Jews and Muslims, but this refuge is temporary and ends in disgrace.
rows.anchor: they claim to have protected themselves from both the Jews and the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadd is used transitively and intransitively; context indicates the intransitive sense of withdrawing after beginning the path of Islam.
rows.anchor: it is evident that it is used in the latter sense: they did take a step forward towards Islam but then withdrew from this path

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke calls their supposedly clever diplomacy a foolish scheme that will bring doom.
rows.anchor: in the eyes of God, this is an absolutely foolish scheme which will lead them to doom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s practice is to increase the light of those who value it, but to withdraw it and seal the hearts of those who retract from faith, depriving them of right understanding; the reasons for the Jews’ sealing are detailed in al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: if people who are shown the light of Islam by Him, and value and honour this light

rows.speaker: Jesus (sws)
rows.claim: Islahi invokes Jesus’ saying that even what people possess can be taken away as a parallel to the loss of spiritual light (Matthew 13:12).
rows.anchor: Jesus (sws) had said: “even what they have with them is taken away.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four brief sentences first portray the hypocrites’ outward appearance and then disclose their inner selves; the Prophet is later told to beware of them, with pity for their condition.
rows.anchor: The first two sentences depict their outer personalities and the last two describe their inner ones

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attractive bodies reflect affluence gained lawfully and unlawfully, and their stinginess leaves them unwilling to support religious and collective needs; Ibn Ubayy leads a wealthy group.
rows.anchor: these hypocrites were affluent. In the first place, they had amassed riches through both lawful and unlawful means

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their persuasive speeches defend Islam and win listeners, but their earlier boasts of jihad collapse when action is required; the gracious Prophet still hears them.
rows.anchor: they would speak so effectively in the support and defence of Islam that they would win the hearts of their addressees

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The timber image depicts attractive but hollow figures whose hearts are dead and sealed, as the preceding verse states.
rows.anchor: even though they have attractive appearances, their hearts are dead

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣayḥah literally means a shout but here means danger; the cowards imagine every danger will fall on them.
rows.anchor: here, it is used in this latter sense

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites deflect suspicion onto others and blame innocent Muslims for crimes they themselves commit, though they are Islam’s real enemies and the Prophet must beware.
rows.anchor: they themselves are in fact the real enemies of Islam, and, as such, the Prophet (sws) should always beware of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer that God destroy them both rebukes and pities them as people repeatedly misled into wrong steps.
rows.anchor: chide them as well as express pity on them: may God destroy them; how misled are they

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links this hypocritical pattern to al-Baqarah’s portrait of people whose pleasing talk masks enmity, corruption, and arrogant sin.
rows.anchor: whereas, in fact, they are the deadliest among the enemies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi states that arrogance brings the punishment of God’s refusal to guide the persistently disobedient.
rows.anchor: Stated here is the punishment of their arrogance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says hypocrites are so worthy of wrath that God will not forgive them even if the Messenger seeks forgiveness seventy times.
rows.anchor: so angered is He of them, that He will not forgive them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verdict is that God does not guide those who persist in disobedience; He guides those ashamed of sin who turn to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: He guides only those who are ashamed of their sins, and turn to the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nisāʾ 4:64 says wrongdoers who come to the Prophet and seek pardon, with his prayer for them, would find God forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: they would have found God forgiving and merciful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the arrogant, al-Tawbah 9:80 says seeking forgiveness seventy times will not secure pardon.
rows.anchor: It is the same whether or not you seek forgiveness for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some narratives place a fight between a poor Muhājir and an Anṣārī at a spring where the Prophet’s army stopped in Banī Muṣṭaliq in 6 AH; Abdullah ibn Ubayy seized the occasion to incite the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: a fight took place between a poor muhājir and an anṣārī at the spring

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Ubayy compared the Muhājirūn to a dog that bites its benefactor, urged the Anṣār to stop helping them, and said they would expel them on return.
rows.anchor: if a person feeds a dog and it becomes strong, then it will bite that very person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes hearts so full of hatred and venom toward Islam and Muslims that they are unworthy of pardon.
rows.anchor: how can God forgive such people whose hearts are filled with such hate and venom against Islam and Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership of heaven’s and earth’s treasures answers the hypocrites’ claim that withholding support would leave the Messenger’s followers helpless; sealed hearts cannot grasp this.
rows.anchor: all the treasures of the heavens and the earth are in the possession of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited divine practice promises that God and His messengers will prevail over those who oppose them.
rows.anchor: has decreed: “I will indeed triumph, and My messengers.” Indeed, powerful is God, the Mighty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims are warned not to copy hypocrites whose love of wealth and children makes them forget God and the Hereafter, which is true loss and Satan’s faction.
rows.anchor: The love of wealth and children has made them indifferent to God; they have no resolve left in them to do something for the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The way to preserve remembrance and resist wealth, family, and hypocrisy is to spend God’s provision for the Hereafter before death.
rows.anchor: Every person should try, before his own death, to earn whatever he can for the Hereafter by spending for the cause of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites had clenched their fists from miserliness; when poor they had promised to give generously if enriched, then broke that promise.
rows.anchor: they would keep clenching their fists because of miserliness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawbah 9:75–77 recounts people who pledged charity if God enriched them, but became miserly and turned away when He fulfilled their wish.
rows.anchor: So, when God bestowed His blessing on them, they became stingy and turned away by being unmindful.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As punishment for their broken promise, God bolstered hypocrisy in their hearts.
rows.anchor: So as a punishment, God bolstered hypocrisy in their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥadīd’s account says charitable people will be raised among the righteous, including the truthful and witnesses, with a light guiding them to Paradise.
rows.anchor: which will include the truthful and the witnesses to the truth and a light will accompany them and lead them to Paradise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary on al-Ḥadīd says those who withhold charity are marked by hypocrisy, lack the light that leads the righteous to Paradise, and will yearn for what they omitted.
rows.anchor: those who desist in this world from spending in charity not only become distinct from the righteous among believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the second verb is apparently coordinated with the accusative fa-aṣṣaddaqa, but Islahi reads it as the answer to a suppressed condition: had I given charity, I would be righteous.
rows.anchor: the expression و is the answer to a suppressed condition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deathbed wish for time remains futile: God does not extend a soul’s term, and He knows that the promise of future charity is baseless.
rows.anchor: Once the respite of life given by God expires, He does not extend it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Taghābun continues al-Munāfiqūn’s warning about wealth, children, charity, and death: worldly life is not final, and the Hereafter reveals success or failure.
rows.anchor: In this sūrah, the same subject is the central theme, and it is explained that this worldly life is not all that there is

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To attain the Hereafter’s great success, one must be ready to sacrifice for God and His Messenger despite reproach; family love may weaken resolve, so regard family as a trial while forgiving them.
rows.anchor: it is mandatory upon one who has the resolve to achieve the great success of the Hereafter, to be prepared for every sacrifice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and its sustaining care are purposeful evidence that a reckoning is appointed; God knows each person’s words and deeds and will judge according to merit.
rows.anchor: The great effort undertaken by the Almighty in His creation to sustain and nourish him bears witness that the Day of Reckoning has an appointed time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations rejected warnings of the Hereafter and sound prophetic arguments, treating a human prophet as an insult; God destroyed them in this world and will punish them in the next.
rows.anchor: nations which denied the warnings of their respective prophets about the Hereafter and vainly rejected their sound arguments

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are urged to believe in God, His Prophet, and the Qur’an and prepare for the Day that decides victor and vanquished.
rows.anchor: People are invited to profess faith in God, His Prophet (sws) and the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering day distinguishes winners from losers: believers who do good receive eternal Paradise, while disbelievers who reject revelation remain in Hell.
rows.anchor: eternal reward of paradise, while He will cast those who adhered to disbelief in the eternal torment of Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardships occur by God’s permission; believers should trust Him and keep obeying rather than evade God and the Prophet, while the Prophet’s duty is clear communication and theirs is adherence.
rows.anchor: It is not befitting for the believers to become apprehensive because of them and turn away from the obedience of God and His Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Family can test faith and weaken religious resolve, so its desires must not restrain religious duty; nevertheless, believers should forgive, overlook, and pardon family.
rows.anchor: their love or their desires should not restrain him in the cause of religion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are invited to obey God and His Prophet to the extent they can.
rows.anchor: People are invited to obey God and His Prophet (sws) as much as they can

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generous spending and freedom from miserliness lead to eternal success; God will multiply the wealth lent to Him and forgive the donors.
rows.anchor: Glad tidings are given of eternal success to those who protect themselves from the malady of miserliness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the seen and unseen and is fully aware of virtuous deeds done in secret.
rows.anchor: He is fully aware of all virtuous deeds, however secretly they might have been done
